title: Rigveda 9.34: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.34: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.34 is a hymn of 6 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 680r-680v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 9.34.1-2 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 8, varga 24); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 680r
translation.original_text:
1pra su̍vā̱no dhāra̍yā̱ tanendu̍r hinvā̱no a̍rṣati | ru̱jad dṛ̱ḻhā vy oja̍sā ||
2su̱ta indrā̍ya vā̱yave̱ varu̍ṇāya ma̱rudbhya̍ḥ | somo̍ arṣati̱ viṣṇa̍ve ||
translation.text:
1THE drop of Soma juice effused flows onward with this stream impelled. Rending strong places with its might.
2Poured forth to Indra, Varuṇa, to Vâyu and the Marut hosts, To Vishṇu, flows the Soma juice.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 680r (numbered 102r by the scribe) (OPenn image 680, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.32.5 ‹yathā hitam›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 680v (numbered 102v by the scribe), begins in RV 9.34.3 ‹duhanti śakmanā payaḥ›. Verses 9.34.1-2 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1pra | suvānaḥ | dhārayā | tanā | induḥ | hinvānaḥ | arṣati | rujat | dṛḷhā | vi | ojasā
2sutaḥ | indrāya | vāyave | varuṇāya | marut-bhyaḥ | somaḥ | arṣati | viṣṇave

translation.original_ref: RV 9.34.3-6 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 8, varga 24); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 680v
translation.original_text:
3vṛṣā̍ṇa̱ṁ vṛṣa̍bhir ya̱taṁ su̱nvanti̱ soma̱m adri̍bhiḥ | du̱hanti̱ śakma̍nā̱ paya̍ḥ ||
4bhuva̍t tri̱tasya̱ marjyo̱ bhuva̱d indrā̍ya matsa̱raḥ | saṁ rū̱pair a̍jyate̱ hari̍ḥ ||
5a̱bhīm ṛ̱tasya̍ vi̱ṣṭapa̍ṁ duha̱te pṛśni̍mātaraḥ | cāru̍ pri̱yata̍maṁ ha̱viḥ ||
6sam e̍na̱m ahru̍tā i̱mā giro̍ arṣanti sa̱sruta̍ḥ | dhe̱nūr vā̱śro a̍vīvaśat ||
translation.text:
3With stones they press the Soma forth, the Strong conducted by the strong: They milk the liquor out with skill.
4'Tis he whom Trita must refine, 'tis he who shall make Indra glad: The Tawny One is decked with tints.
5Him do the Sons of Pr̥iṣni milk, the dwelling-place of sacrifice, Oblation lovely and most dear.
6To him in one united stream these songs flow on straight forward. he, Loud voiced, hath made the milch-kine low.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 680v (numbered 102v by the scribe) (OPenn image 681, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.34.3 ‹duhanti śakmanā payaḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 681r (numbered 103r by the scribe), begins in RV 9.36.1 ‹vājī ni akramīt›. Verses 9.34.3-6 end on this page; 9.34.3 begins on fol. 680r (numbered 102r by the scribe).
translation.edition_text:
3vṛṣāṇam | vṛṣa-bhiḥ | yatam | sunvanti | somam | adri-bhiḥ | duhanti | śakmanā | payaḥ
4bhuvat | tritasya | marjyaḥ | bhuvat | indrāya | matsaraḥ | sam | rūpaiḥ | ajyate | hariḥ
5abhi | īm | ṛtasya | viṣṭapam | duhate | pṛśni-mātaraḥ | cāru | priya-tamam | haviḥ
6sam | enam | ahutāḥ | imāḥ | giraḥ | arṣanti | sa-srutaḥ | dhenūḥ | vāśraḥ | avīvaśan
